title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
read_level: full (PDF via pdftotext, incl. appendices; figure values read from extracted figure text)
why_wsp: GPT-6 Astra inspects Qwen3.5 weights in a Python kernel and writes gradient-free edits (column, rank-one, head ablation/scaling), testing them with a 50-request forward budget.
domain: LLM math reasoning, science QA, instruction following, scientific coding
self_editing: no; editor (Astra) edits a separate Qwen3.5 model
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "modifying only 1,023 parameters yields a 29.45-point improvement" (Abstract); other edits range to 41,054,142 BF16 values (9B MMLU-Pro, Table 6)

headline_results.quote: accuracy improves by up to 29.45, 4.42, 36.72, and 17.11 percentage points on MATH-500, GPQA Diamond, IFEval, and SciBench, respectively
A Math-edited checkpoint improves GPQA Diamond, IFEval, and SciBench by 3.03, 12.18, and 20.10 points, respectively, without further editing, while leaving SciCode performance unchanged
the primary search achieves a +29.45 percentage-point improvement, while reruns 1 and 2 yield gains of +5.00 and +27.30 points

headline_results.claim: Edit size does not predict gain
headline_results.quote: rerun 1 modifies 1,037,572 values through a rank-one update but yields only +5.00 points, while rerun 2 changes 1,981,083 values and achieves +27.30 points
six of the 16 trajectories retain the original weights when candidate improvements cannot be reliably validated
the evaluated 9B Math candidate decreases held-out accuracy by 0.35 points, despite a +29.69-point development gain

The targeted edit with α = 1 reaches 20 of 48, and ablation gives 4 of 48. The reversed direction with α = −0.5 gives 0 of 48, and a single random direction orthogonal to u with equal norm gives 10 of 48

cost.claim: Search budget: 50 forward requests, up to 300 Python analyses
cost.quote: Forward budget 50 successful requests; G and TF requests each count once ... Python analyses At most 300 per search

cost.claim: Cost noted qualitatively; no tokens/$ reported
cost.quote: repeated evaluations incur substantial computational costs

baselines_and_controls: Base (unedited) checkpoint under matched held-out evaluation; within primary MATH search: channel ablation, reversed direction, one equal-norm orthogonal random direction, dose sweep. No fine-tuning/LoRA/prompting baseline.
runs_and_variance: One trajectory per model-benchmark pair, except 0.8B MATH with 3 independent searches (+29.45, +5.00, +27.30). Held-out final eval seed 0; paired SE formula given (App. B) but CIs not tabulated in main results. "Development results are selected adaptively and are reported without correction for multiple comparisons."
robustness_of_edits: not tested (no fine-tuning/quantization tests); cross-task transfer evaluated (Fig. 6), mixed: 'transfer is not uniformly beneficial'
verification: none (statistical paired comparison on held-out sets only)
memorization_vs_reasoning: Prompt states 'new independent experiment with no previous edits, notes, trajectories or published editing recipe'; editor's primary edit targets doubt-vs-progress token direction (loop repair), similar to original WSP finding. No direct test of memorization.
limitations_stated: Outcomes vary across trajectories; 50-request budget sometimes insufficient to validate edits; dev gains do not always transfer to held-out; mechanisms of success unclear; not evaluated on long-horizon/agentic tasks; one trajectory per pair.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al., Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (MIT CSAIL blog, 2026-11-02)
notes_for_survey: Replication/extension of the original WSP Qwen loop-repair setup across 7 benchmarks and 2 scales with full edit specifications in appendix. Gains concentrate on 0.8B (low baseline, truncation-driven failures); 9B gains are within a few points and 4 of 7 9B searches kept original weights. Three MATH reruns land on the same tensor (layer-23 down_proj) with different structures and gains.
